sources.note: 480 speakers (2003 SIL), East Sepik; dialects none known; related to Changriwa, Mekmek, Biwat, Kyenele. Nothing linguistic.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bunn1240 and hh.bib (held by the project at _glottolog_bib/hh.bib): entries with language code [buv]
sources.note: Only four items carry the buv code: Laycock 1973, Laycock Notebook D34, Foley 2005 and McDowell 1975 (ethnographic); Glottolog counts 0 descriptive references; Foley 2018 is cited for subclassification only.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In A. Pawley, R. Attenborough, J. Golson & R. Hide (eds.), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Pacific Linguistics 572. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146735; whole-volume PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 126: 'The Yuat languages are very poorly known; I only have data on three of them: Biwat, Bun and Miyak.. Biwat and Bun possibly being dialects of one language'; uses pronouns and plural -bi only. No phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38. (hdl 1885/252975)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phylum-wide list of widespread features (p. 732) includes 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems' for the Sepik-Ramu phylum as a whole; sec. 2.11.3.5.1 Yuat Super-Stock (p. 758) is classification only. No Bun data, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146478; DOI 10.15144/PL-B25)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Yuat stock paragraph (pp. 36-37) is typological/lexical only (plural marking phonologically predictable, no noun classification, no person marking); entry 131 BUN (p. 37): village Bun, test list DCL71, 'Almost, but not quite, a dialect of Biwat.' Nothing on stress; the only prosody remark in the book (p. 5) concerns Sissano/Warapu tone.

sources.note: No record for buv; the only 'Yuat' hit is Comrie & Davies 1985 'A linguistic survey of the Upper Yuat' (Haruai/Pinai area, not the Yuat family). No SIL phonology/survey exists for Bun.

sources.citation: McElvenny, James. 2006. Draft sketch grammar of Biwat (Mudukumo/Mundugumor), a Yuat language of East Sepik Province, PNG [= Notes on the Mudukumo language of the Yuat River]. University of Sydney, unpublished MS, 62 pp.

sources.note: The only descriptive phonology of any Yuat language; Barlow 2023 cites its phoneme statements. Would give the stress rule for Biwat, the closest relative and possible co-dialect of Bun; not on any open repository.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: The only modern published treatment of the Yuat family; its Yuat section gives a Mundukumo/Biwat phoneme inventory and may carry a prosody remark applicable to Bun (Biwat and Bun are near-dialects per Laycock 1973 and Foley 2005).
